target: USWDS modal mobile, scrolling, content length and clear action-label warnings
observed_behavior: USWDS identifies default and large modal sizes, suggesting the large version or a separate page when content cannot fit without scrolling. It cautions that long text can push actions out of the initially visible area and asks authors to clarify that more content is scrollable. It advises minimizing controls beyond buttons because nested forms or accordions can lose context on mobile, keeping button text specific about consequences, avoiding unexpected automatic dialogs with limited situational exceptions, and not blocking outbound links with additional exit-confirmation dialogs. It also recommends that dismissing a modal leave the underlying page unchanged rather than reloading it.
context: W07 B4 K3 bounded first-party USWDS Modal reference; source sections: About the modal component; Usability guidance; When to consider something else. Explanatory DESIGN_SYSTEM / OFFICIAL_REFERENCE only; not cross-source or runtime evidence.
limitations: The source provides product-context advice, not a measured mobile layout or universal pixel/viewport threshold.
USWDS provides two named modal variants; selecting one or requiring a particular width in Kirion is not authorized.
Warnings about form fields and accordions do not establish that every modal form is impossible or always inaccessible.
The advice on avoiding automatic dialogs has examples such as session-timeout notices or initial consent as contextual exceptions.
No phone, orientation, zoom, scroll, focus restoration, link-navigation or usability test was run.
